item.title: Rethinking Agentic Model Orchestration for Time Series Forecasting
item.description: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) perform unevenly across forecasting tasks. Recent work uses agentic model orchestration (AMO) to select or combine TSFMs, often outperforming individual forecasters. Yet these gains may reflect stronger or more complementary candidates rather than better orchestration. To disentangle these effects, we introduce FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol with frozen candidate forecasts. item.description: Omni-modal large language models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in audio and video understanding. However, existing models struggle with long-form, multi-speaker videos, especially in understanding the entire video and recognizing who says what and when. item.title: Extending Affordance Segmentation for Wearable Robots to Multi-Object Images
item.description: This paper proposes a refinement to existing vision-based portable pipelines for the recognition of graspable object parts. Such pipelines can effectively support automatic grasp selection and preshaping in upper-limb prosthetic devices. However, realistic scenarios in which multiple objects are present still represent a challenge. The proposed method exploits a minor modification to the conventional hardware setup and a custom training approach to extend the applicability of vision-based pipelines. A laser pointer is introduced in the setup as an effective mechanism for object disambiguation. — 来源：simonwillison · arxiv — 原文：https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.29474v1

item.title: Agentic World Action Models
item.description: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. item.title: Do Earth-Trained Humanoid Controllers Walk on the Moon? Gravity, Terrain, and Soil Transfer
item.description: The Moon changes gravity, terrain, and soil at once. item.description: Humanoid loco-manipulation requires an effective interface between high-level task policies and whole-body control.
